newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN COMPANY SLAMS AZOMURES CONTRACT ANNULLMENT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN COMPANY SLAMS AZOMURES CONTRACT ANNULLMENT.

text.p: Romanian trader Euro Trading protested on Friday over the cancellation of a deal to buy a stake in Azomures fertiliser maker due to failure to pay despite a court ruling suspending payment for six months.
"Euro Trading Chemicals considers the State Ownership Fund (FPS) cannot annul the contract unilaterally," a company statement said.
The FPS, which has a control stake in most Romanian state companies, said it had cancelled sale of 51 percent of Azomures to Euro Trading after its failure to meet a payment deadline.
It said it would reopen Azomures selloff negotiations with a second bidder -- local trading company Omnimpex Chemicals.

Euro Trading had won a February tender for Azomures shares in a bidding which triggered an investigation by Romania's main competition superviser into a possible "economic concentration" in the fertiliser industry.
Euro Trading already has stakes in another two fertiliser makers. It says the Azomures purchase would put its stake of the Romanian fertiliser industry at about 42 percent.
Euro Trading spokesman Remus Vulpescu said his company had asked a Bucharest court to rule on payment suspension pending the results of the Competition Coucil's investigation.
The ruling suspended payment for the Azomures shares, as well as a clause under the contract with the FPS saying the deal could be annulled on failure to pay, Euro Trading said.
The FPS said on Friday it had not been notified of the court ruling.
"We could lodge a complaint in court the moment the FPS starts new (Azomures) selloff procedures," Vulpescu said.
The FPS said it would reach a decision on Azomures' selloff as soon as it got the court ruling.
Azomures, which has a capital of 209.5 billion lei, has been a most heavily traded stock ever since it joined the bourse last January. ($=7,110 lei)
